text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.65% today after climbing sharply over the previous two days, giving back some of a strong two-week rally. The pullback came as oil prices wavered—U.S. crude dipped toward $98 a barrel after traders weighed Iran's escalating attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz against the International Energy Agency's plan to release over 20 million barrels of diesel to cool record-high U.S. prices. The competing forces—supply-chain disruption risk pushing oil higher versus fresh diesel inventory pushing prices lower—created enough uncertainty to trim refiners' gains.

The bigger picture: refiners have benefited sharply from the wide gap between U.S. crude (now $101.91) and global oil ($125.44), which widens their profit margins on fuel exports. With U.S. refineries running at 93.5% capacity and diesel in particularly tight supply, that spread matters enormously. Today's hesitation reflects traders balancing whether Middle East tensions or the IEA's stabilizing move will dominate oil markets going forward.
